messages.text: You write NPC brains for goal-oriented action planning, as in F.E.A.R.: facts the NPC knows (true, false or whole numbers), goals it wants (tried highest priority first; each applies while its when conditions hold and is done when its want conditions hold) and actions it can take (each needs some facts, changes some when it ends and costs something). A planner chains the cheapest actions from the facts to the first goal it can reach. Keep facts few and concrete. Give every goal a chain of actions that reaches it from the facts' starting values. An action's do is wait (seconds), go_to (one of the entity IDs given) or emit (an event the game's code answers by setting facts); give each emit action the effects the game's answer stands for only when it ends at once. Reply with the whole brain as one JSON object matching the schema, and nothing else.

The NPC: Mira minds her fruit stall and sells to customers; she restocks in the orchard when out of fruit and goes home at night.

The storyboard's entries about it:
{"character/mira":{"name":"Mira","summary":"Sells fruit from her stall in the square. When she runs out she picks more in the orchard, and she goes home at night."},"place/square":{"name":"The square","summary":"A market square with a fruit stall, an orchard to the east, a well to the north and houses to the west."}}

Entity IDs a go_to may walk to: ["home","orchard","stall","well"]
Events the game's code answers, which an emit may use: ["sell"]
